answer: Tie issuance to graded-work history: a new identity earns at a basalt base rate and only climbs as its past answers are graded genuine by unrelated peers. Rewards behave like a prism, splitting newcomers from proven contributors, so an attacker must first do months of honest work per alias before the ember of real payout ignites. Clones stay at the floor rate forever, and flooding the network with them dilutes nothing.
